stories.title: Starcloud raises $250 million for data centers in orbit
stories.summary: Starcloud raised $250 million to build data centers in orbit. Launch capacity is now scarce, and TechCrunch reports this scarcity may be pushing the company toward space. Starcloud aims to run computing hardware outside Earth's atmosphere.
stories.whyItMatters: Space-based data centers could ease the land and power limits that constrain AI growth on Earth.
whatToWatch: A launch date for the first orbital data center
Which launch providers Starcloud uses
Whether rivals announce similar orbital plans
questions: How will Starcloud manage cooling and radiation in orbit?
Who are the investors behind the $250 million round?

sources.title: Starcloud raises $250 million for orbital data centers as launch options dry up

stories.title: Nevada clears Tesla, Uber, and Waymo to run paid robotaxis
stories.summary: Nevada regulators approved Tesla, Uber, and Waymo to run paid robotaxi service in the state. The approval covers thousands of vehicles across the three companies. Nevada now joins a small group of states that allow paid autonomous rides.
stories.whyItMatters: Three major operators now compete under one state's rules, a real test of whether the robotaxi market can support multiple players at once.
whatToWatch: When each company starts paid rides in Nevada
Fleet sizes as service ramps up
Reaction from regulators in other states
questions: Will all three companies launch on the same timeline?
How will Nevada handle safety incidents across three different fleets?

sources.title: Nevada allows Uber, Tesla and Waymo to start paid robotaxi service
Tesla, Uber, and Waymo all get the OK to operate thousands of robotaxis in Nevada

stories.title: Senator asks federal watchdog to review agencies' use of hacking tools
stories.summary: A U.S. senator asked a government watchdog to review how federal agencies use hacking tools. TechCrunch reports the request seeks oversight of tools that let agencies break into devices or networks. Few other details are available yet.
stories.whyItMatters: Oversight of government hacking tools affects how much power federal agencies have over personal devices and data.
whatToWatch: Whether the watchdog agrees to open a review
Any response from the agencies involved
questions: Which senator made the request?
Which agencies and tools does the review target?

stories.title: As demand for Meta's AI glasses grows, so do privacy concerns
stories.summary: Demand for Meta's AI glasses is rising sharply, according to Ars Technica. As more people wear the glasses, bystanders find it harder to know when a camera is recording. The report points to gaps in how the devices signal that they are on.
stories.whyItMatters: Wearable cameras that blend into everyday life raise hard questions about consent and surveillance in public spaces.
whatToWatch: Whether Meta changes recording indicators on the glasses
Any regulatory or lawmaker response to the privacy concerns
questions: What recording indicator does Meta currently use, and is it enough?
Could public pressure force a design change?

sources.title: As demand for Meta AI glasses explodes, it’s harder to avoid creepy recordings

stories.summary: Ars Technica's Rocket Report covers a new SpaceX milestone on the Moon and a new chief executive at United Launch Alliance. The roundup tracks ongoing activity across the launch industry. Full details on both items are limited in the summary available.

whatToWatch: Next moves from ULA's new leadership
Further updates on SpaceX's lunar activity
questions: What exactly did SpaceX accomplish on the Moon?
Who is ULA's new CEO, and what is their background?

stories.title: A new wireless 4K60 HDMI system aims to cut cord clutter
stories.summary: Wired reviewed the Nyrius Phoenix Home True 4K60, a wireless HDMI system meant to reduce cable clutter around TVs and home theater setups. The device sends 4K video at 60 frames per second without a physical HDMI cable run. It targets a common annoyance in home entertainment setups.
stories.whyItMatters: Wireless video transmission is a small but steady front in the push to simplify home entertainment hardware.
questions: How reliable is the wireless connection at longer range or through walls?

stories.title: Pixel Watch 5 review: strong hardware, missing features at launch
stories.summary: Engadget's review of the Pixel Watch 5 calls it a strong smartwatch overall but notes it ships without some features at launch. The device is Google's latest entry in the Wear OS smartwatch line. The review did not specify which features are missing.
stories.whyItMatters: Google's execution on Pixel Watch hardware and software shapes Wear OS's ability to compete with Apple Watch.
whatToWatch: Whether Google adds the missing features through a software update
How the Pixel Watch 5 sells against rival smartwatches
questions: Which specific features are missing at launch?
When might Google fill the gaps?

stories.title: A super El Niño won't solve the West's water crisis, Wired reports
stories.summary: Wired reports that a forecast 'super El Niño' will not resolve the long-term water shortage facing the western United States. The piece treats the wet weather pattern as, at best, a temporary reprieve. Underlying structural water supply issues remain unaddressed.
stories.whyItMatters: Water scarcity in the West affects the power and cooling needs of data centers and other tech infrastructure sited in the region.
questions: How much relief, if any, will this El Niño actually provide?

sources.title: The Super El Niño Won’t Fix the West’s Water Crisis

stories.title: Tesla recalls 3 million cars in China over hidden door handles
stories.summary: Tesla is recalling about 3 million vehicles in China as part of a nationwide push to fix hidden door handles. The handles can be hard to open in an emergency, such as after a crash or loss of power. This is one of Tesla's largest recalls in China to date.
stories.whyItMatters: The recall puts pressure on Tesla's design choices in its biggest market outside the U.S. and raises safety questions for other automakers with similar handles.
whatToWatch: How Tesla implements the fix, by software update or hardware change
Whether regulators in other markets order similar action
questions: Does the fix require a physical part change or just a software update?
Have the hidden handles caused any documented injuries?

sources.title: Tesla recalls 3 million cars as part of China-wide push to stop hidden door handles

stories.title: Top YouTube creators face backlash for taking AI money
stories.summary: Several major YouTube creators face criticism from their audiences after accepting payment tied to AI companies or products, The Verge reports. Viewers have pushed back over concerns about AI's effect on creative work. The backlash reflects wider tension between AI companies and online creator communities.
stories.whyItMatters: Creator backlash over AI sponsorships signals how much trust AI companies still need to build with online audiences.
whatToWatch: Whether affected creators respond publicly or drop the sponsorships
Whether AI companies change how they court creators
questions: Which creators and AI companies are involved?
What exactly are audiences objecting to?

stories.title: Apollo confirms data breach amid hacking wave hitting financial firms
stories.summary: Private equity firm Apollo confirmed a data breach, TechCrunch reports, as part of a broader wave of hacking incidents targeting financial giants. Other firms in finance appear to be targeted in the same wave. The scope of the Apollo breach was not detailed further.
stories.whyItMatters: A hacking wave hitting major financial firms raises the stakes for data security across an industry that holds vast amounts of sensitive financial data.
whatToWatch: Which other financial firms disclose breaches from this wave
What data Apollo confirms was affected
Any regulatory response to the breach wave
questions: Who is behind the hacking wave?
What specific data did the Apollo breach expose?

stories.title: Blue Eye Samurai season 2 arrives on Netflix in January
stories.summary: Netflix confirmed the animated series Blue Eye Samurai will return for a second season in January, The Verge reports. The show is one of Netflix's original animated titles. Netflix gave no further details about the new season's plot.
stories.whyItMatters: Continued investment in original animation is part of Netflix's push to hold subscribers against rival streaming platforms.
